title: Career Roadmap: Third Officer
summary: In India, candidates should verify the current eligibility and certification requirements with the Directorate General of Shipping (DGS) and choose a recognised maritime training institution.

facts.Current degree: Merchant Navy / Maritime Programmes – Deck Cadet / Nautical Science (DNS/B.Sc Nautical)

about.label: Recommended Education
about.text: Diploma in Nautical Science (DNS) or B.Sc. in Nautical Science through an appropriately approved pathway

about.label: Workplaces
about.text: Cargo vessels, container ships, tankers, bulk carriers, passenger ships, and other commercial vessels

about.label: Career Type
about.text: Deck Operations, Navigation, Maritime Safety, Shipboard Operations

blocks.label: Important career note
blocks.text: A Third Officer is a licensed deck officer responsible for assigned navigation, safety, and shipboard duties. This is generally not a direct-entry position immediately after an ordinary undergraduate degree. Candidates typically complete an approved nautical training pathway, required sea service, competency assessments, and the applicable Certificate of Competency (CoC) requirements.
In India, candidates should verify the current eligibility and certification requirements with the Directorate General of Shipping (DGS) and choose a recognised maritime training institution.

A Third Officer, also called a Third Mate on some vessels, is a junior officer in the ship's deck department. The role involves supporting safe navigation, maintaining designated safety equipment, assisting with watchkeeping, and ensuring that assigned shipboard procedures are followed.

The Third Officer works under the authority of the Chief Officer and Master (Captain). Responsibilities vary by vessel type, company procedures, flag-state requirements, and the officer's certification.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Keep a navigational watch when assigned and appropriately qualified.
Monitor the vessel's position, course, speed, and surrounding traffic.
Assist with passage planning and navigation preparation.
Maintain assigned lifesaving and firefighting equipment records and readiness.
Participate in emergency drills and onboard safety activities.
Follow collision-prevention rules and bridge procedures.
Maintain navigational logs and required records.
Assist with safe cargo and deck operations within assigned responsibilities.
Communicate with the bridge team, engine department, and other shipboard personnel.
Report hazards, equipment defects, and incidents through the vessel's established procedures.

blocks.label: Safety comes first
blocks.text: Navigation and watchkeeping duties must be performed in accordance with the officer's certification, applicable maritime regulations, company procedures, and the Master's orders.

blocks.text: These are illustrative career stages, not guaranteed dates. Promotion depends on sea service, competency examinations, medical fitness, employer requirements, and the relevant Certificate of Competency.
The academic route differs between DNS and B.Sc. Nautical Science.

blocks.label: DNS
blocks.text: Typically combines pre-sea training with structured shipboard training.

blocks.label: B.Sc. Nautical Science
blocks.text: Provides a longer academic programme followed by the required sea service and competency pathway.
The current official Indian maritime guidance describes these routes and their certification requirements. Always check the latest entry criteria before applying.

Year 1 — Nautical and Maritime Foundations
Subjects to learn
Practical development

items.text: Learn nautical terminology and bridge communication.
Understand ropes, knots, mooring equipment, and deck tools.
Study shipboard hierarchy and professional discipline.

blocks.text: Build the foundation required for professional nautical training.
Year 2 — Navigation and Shipboard Operations
Subjects to learn
Practical development

items.text: Practise plotting courses and positions on training charts.
Learn cargo documentation and basic stowage concepts.
Participate in approved safety and survival training.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Understand the technical principles behind navigation, cargo operations, and ship safety.
Year 3 — Advanced Nautical Training
Applicable mainly to students in a three-year B.Sc. programme; DNS students should follow their approved course and sea-training schedule.

Year 4 — Sea Service and Professional Qualification
This stage is not necessarily a fourth university year. It represents the subsequent professional pathway where applicable.

blocks.text: Safety is the primary priority. Performance should never be measured by speed alone or by avoiding incident reports.

blocks.text: Projects should use educational scenarios, simulators, and publicly available material. They do not replace approved maritime training or competency assessments.
Use the following five-point scale:

items.text: 4/5: Can perform independently within the limits of qualification and authorisation
5/5: Can lead, assess, and improve performance at the appropriate professional level

blocks.text: These are educational targets, not official examination scores or substitutes for formal competency assessments.
For a nautical career, approved sea service is a core part of professional qualification—not simply an optional internship.

blocks.text: Recommended progression

items.text: Verify eligibility for DNS or B.Sc. Nautical Science.
Confirm the maritime training institute's current approval status.
Investigate company sponsorship and cadet berth arrangements.
Complete the required onboard sea service and training record book.
Complete prescribed safety, communication, and competency courses.
Obtain the relevant Certificate of Competency.
Apply for a suitable junior deck officer appointment.

blocks.text: For foreign-going watchkeeping officer certification, India's official nautical guidance identifies approved training, sea service, bridge watchkeeping, and competency assessments as essential requirements.

sections.heading: Target Profile Before Becoming a Third Officer

blocks.text: The candidate should aim to have:

items.text: Completed the relevant approved nautical education pathway.
Completed required pre-sea and safety training.
Acquired the prescribed sea service and documented onboard training.
Demonstrated competency in navigation and bridge watchkeeping.
Completed required examinations and specialist courses.
Met applicable medical and certification requirements.
Obtained the relevant Certificate of Competency.
Developed strong maritime English, teamwork, and safety discipline.
Secured an appropriate junior deck officer appointment.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Completing DNS or B.Sc. Nautical Science alone does not automatically qualify someone for appointment as a Third Officer.

Approved DNS/B.Sc. Nautical Science pathway → pre-sea training → Deck Cadet sea service → required STCW training and competency assessments → relevant Certificate of Competency → junior deck officer appointment → Second Officer → Chief Officer → Master (Captain).
